steps.prompt: Why does the guest say “I’d like to check in” and not “I want to check in”?
options: I’d like to is the polite form for a service situation.
I want is grammatically wrong in this kind of sentence.
There is no difference at all between the two sentences.
steps.answer: I’d like to is the polite form for a service situation.
steps.why: I’d like, Could you …? and Is there …? are the standard polite forms with strangers.

steps.title: At the reception desk
steps.html:
What you wantWhat you say
arrivingI’d like to check in, please. / I have a reservation under …
asking about a serviceIs Wi-Fi available in the room? / Is there a charge for it?
asking for somethingCould we have a spare towel, please? / Is there somewhere we can leave our luggage?
asking about timesWhat time is breakfast? / What time is checkout?
not understandingSorry, what was the name again? / Could you say that again?
a problem with the roomI’m afraid there’s a problem with … / Could you send someone up?
the receptionistCould you fill in the registration form, please? / I’ll get someone to help you.

I’d like = I would like. It is followed by to + base form, or by a noun: I’d like to check in / I’d like a double room.

Could you …? is the normal polite request. Can you …? is fine with friends, less so with strangers.

I’m afraid softens bad news in both directions: the guest and the receptionist both use it.

Note the indefinite pronoun from the last lesson doing real work: Is there somewhere we can leave our luggage? I’ll get someone to help you.

The same complaint pattern comes back in Unit 10, Lesson 30, in a restaurant.

steps.title: Notes and messages · model
steps.sub: Three short pieces of writing a traveller sends. You will write your own at the end.
steps.html:
Three short messages from one trip

1 · A note left at reception

Room 206. I’m out until about six. Could you ask housekeeping to bring two more towels? There’s only one in the bathroom. Thank you. — L. Meyer

2 · A message to the hotel before arriving

Good afternoon. I have a reservation for tonight under the name Sarsenova. I’m afraid my train is late and I won’t arrive until about eleven. Is that a problem? Also, is there somewhere I can leave a bag in the morning after checkout? Many thanks.

3 · A message to a friend in the same hotel

Hi — I’ve checked in. Room 411, fourth floor. Breakfast is between seven and ten in the restaurant on the ground floor. Wi-Fi is free of charge but you need a code — it’s on the desk in the room. See you at eight.
